1.mascotDialogue: Same values, two views — a tree for the ordering rule, an array for how she really lives in memory. parent(i) equals (i minus one) over two. The whole address book, tesoro.

2.mascotDialogue: Line 3, this is the bridge between array and tree — any index's parent is always (i-1)/2, integer division. Line 4 is the min-heap rule herself — stop the moment the parent is already smaller or equal.

3.mascotDialogue: Hover index 4 in the array — watch her tree node light up as a child of index 1! Same data, two windows, both singing the same song.

4.mascotDialogue: Both the array cell and the tree node light up in the same broken color at once — because it is one violation, only seen two ways.
